subject: Acme SIG: audit events evidence + temporary retention exception
messages:
From: security@acme-payments.com
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up: audit log events, retention, and customer access

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for taking the time on the SIG earlier. Acme's procurement team asked for a few follow-ups we couldn't cover live. Can you provide the following so we can close our security review?

1) A sample export (CSV) of the tenant audit events covering: authentication events, model invocation events, config change events and admin actions for the last 90 days (PII scrubbed). We only need a representative sample, not full records.

2) The official retention policy excerpt that states default retention windows for tenant-level audit logs, retention controls available to customers, and any supported exceptions.

3) Documentation/steps for how a customer can access their own event logs (API, presigned S3, support-run export), including RBAC and how long those exports remain available.

4) There is a specific ask: Acme requires 12 months of audit events for the financial controls team. Redwood's public docs reference 90 days by default; can you confirm whether a temporary or contract-level retention exception to 12 months is possible for this customer? If not possible, please propose mitigations (e.g., scheduled exports, cost estimate, or escrow).

We'd like to get this package by EOD Friday (2027-05-21) if possible. If you need a narrower scope for the sample, tell us what makes sense.

Thanks,
Maria Gonzales
Security Program Manager
Acme Payments

[attachment: acme_sig_request.pdf (pdf, 200KB)]

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: SIG follow-up: audit log events, retention, and customer access

Jordan — thanks for the ping. Summary of what I pulled together and next steps below.

What we can provide (attached):
- redwood_audit_log_sample.csv — a 14-day sample (PII removed) with fields: timestamp, tenant_id, user_id (hashed), event_type, event_subtype, request_id, resource_path, outcome.
- retention_policy_excerpt_v2.pdf — excerpt from our platform policy showing default tenant audit retention (90 days), archive offerings and policy for retention exceptions.
- short_access_instructions.txt (inline below) describing API export -> presigned S3 flow.

Short access instructions (customer-facing):
1) Customers may retrieve tenant logs via the Redwood Audit Export API (POST /v1/audit/exports) which creates a time-bound S3 export.
2) Exports are delivered as gzipped CSV to a presigned S3 URL; default TTL = 7 days. Support can request a re-run.
3) For continuous forwarding, we support SIEM integration (syslog/forwarding) as a separate add-on.

Retention exception feasibility:
- Default platform retention = 90 days. We can offer a contract-level retention extension in two ways:
  a) Managed extension: Redwood will allocate object storage for this tenant to retain 12 months of parsed audit events. This requires an enterprise addendum (storage charge + SLA for retrieval).
  b) Export escrow: we can schedule automated monthly exports to a customer-owned S3 bucket or to an encrypted Redwood-managed archive; cost is smaller but retrieval is "on request".

Estimated ops impact (very rough): 12-month raw parsed CSVs for an average-financial-tenant = ~120GB/month -> ~1.4TB/year. Additional costs: storage, periodic integrity checks, and retention policy management. We need Legal/Finance approval for a binding exception.

Attachments: redwood_audit_log_sample.csv (14-day sample), retention_policy_excerpt_v2.pdf, evidence-pack-readme.txt

Let me know if you want me to prepare a one-page acceptance checklist for Acme to sign — would make Legal easier.

Lauren Bishop
Product Security, Redwood Inference
